newsitem.title: UK: Moscow has lion's share of investment in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Moscow has lion's share of investment in Russia.

text.p: The City of Moscow attracted 66 percent of foreign investment in Russia in 1996, Moscow's vice-mayor Valery Shantsev told bankers at a conference on Friday.
"The $4.3 billion of foreign investments in Moscow in 1996 accounted for 66 percent of the total Russian foreign investment," said Shantsev, who is also Moscow's first deputy prime minster.
Moscow's share of Russian industrial production grew to 5.7 percent in 1996 from 4.1 percent in 1992, he said.
In the same period, Moscow increased its share of Russian consumer goods production to 9.6 percent from 8.2 percent, Shantsev said.
Despite this, Moscow did not have enough funds for its plans in terms of transportation, communications, tourism, leisure, and construction, he said.
A delegation from Moscow is on an international roadshow ahead of the launch of its debut Eurobond, likely to be a three-year deal worth up to $400 million.
Shantsev said domestic sources of funding, particularly Moscow's tax regime were "imperfect".
"Our tax system is cumbersome but we are adjusting our tax base all the time."
Ioseph Ordjonokidze, head of Moscow's foreign department, said it wanted to help small and medium-sized businesses who contributed significantly to Moscow's economy.
